newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND VALENCIA LOOK TO REVAMP CHALLENGES IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND VALENCIA LOOK TO REVAMP CHALLENGES IN SPAIN.

text.p: Last season's top two will hope to get their championship challenges back on course as Valencia take on Atletico Madrid in this weekend's top game in Spain.
Last season the fixture produced some classic games in both league and cup competitions, but this year's fixture will be played without the key figures from those clashes.

A series of injuries to playmaker Jose Luis Caminero has blighted Atletico's start to the season, while Valencia have been unable to fill the gap left by brilliant Yugoslavian midfielder Predrag Mijatovic, who has moved to Real Madrid.
After just seven matches reigning champions Atletico are already six points behind leaders Barcelona, with Valencia a further point back.
But although Caminero and Mijatovic may be absent, some of the tension generated between the two sides last year is still very much present.
Atletico's epic 5-3 cup victory at Valencia ended with a fist-fight between Bulgarian striker Lyuboslav Penev and Valencia chairman Paco Roig which soured the relationship between the clubs.
Juan Eduardo Esnaider has since replaced Penev in the Atletico attack, but the Argentine international is known for producing fireworks both on and off the ball.

Despite his temperament problems, Esnaider has come up with the goods for Atletico owner Jesus Gil, something that cannot be said for Roig's big close-season signing, another combustible South America, World Cup star Romario.
The striker went back to Brazil earlier in the week, as negotiations continue for his return to Rio de Janeiro club Flamengo.
Gabriel Moya has blossomed in the absence of Romario, and the former Sevilla forward was again on target in Valencia's midweek UEFA Cup win at Slavia Prague.
Atletico's own fine European form was dented by a 1-0 Champions' League defeat by Borussia Dortmund. But, says coach Radomir Antic, morale has not suffered as a result.
"The best side doesn't always win," said Antic the morning after the game, from which Atletico deserved at least a draw, "It's difficult to have so much superiority and lose."
Antic hopes to have Roberto Solozabal, Diego Simeone and Milinko Pantic fit after picking up knocks in the Borussia game, while Valencia are still without influential club captain Francisco Camarasa.
